chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The believer is the brother of the believer, his eye and his guide; he does not betray him, nor oppress him, nor deceive him, nor promise him a promise then break it.
ai.seo_question: What are the key ethical duties of a believer towards his brother in faith according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni presents this hadith as a foundational definition of *ukhuwwah* (brotherhood), framing the believer as the 'eye' and 'guide' of another, which implies mutual spiritual oversight and reliance. The four prohibitions—betrayal, oppression, deception, and broken promises—highlight the comprehensive nature of trust (*amanah*) required in Shia social ethics, extending beyond mere loyalty to include integrity in word and deed. This narration underscores that true faith manifests in consistent, reliable conduct within the community of believers.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali Bin Uqba,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Momin is a brother of the Momin, his eye and his guide, neither betraying, nor oppressing him, nor deceiving him, nor promising him with a promise, then opposing him’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Faddal from Ali ibn ‘Uqbah from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

The believer is a brother (in belief) of a believer, his eyes and his guide. He does not violate his trust, does not do injustice to him, or deceive him, and does not promise him only to ignore it later on.”’
